release_contents: Recruitment application status-change email: VolunteerApplicationStatusChangedNotification, dispatched from JobApplicationController::updateStatus() when an application moves INTO accepted or not_selected. Mirrors MembershipApplicationStatusChangedNotification's shape (on-demand mail route, support@ Reply-To, Bengali copy, try/catch + Log::warning) with three deliberate differences: (1) no note parameter at all, so the internal note cannot reach the message; (2) sent only on a real status transition, so re-saving an already-accepted application does not email again; (3) only the two outcome states notify, not under_review/contacted/shortlisted/withdrawn/archived. Posting title read withTrashed. 14 new tests (387 total), mutation-checked. docs/MAIL_ROLES.md's application-status row names volunteer applications. No correction-request workflow, no pagination change.

switch_note: Clean switch at 2026-09-21T09:55:03Z: ok:true, atomic_rename_ms 5.943, public_asset_sync_ms 18.8, routes_changed false so route:cache correctly skipped, all other cache rebuilds exit 0. The switch cron was armed by the previous Claude session, whose transcript ended before the arming call's result was recorded; the next session found the entry still listed ~1h after it had fired, read its output (ok:true), deleted it, and confirmed the slate empty. A date-specific cron entry stays armed for a year — always delete a fired one-shot, and after any session interruption LIST the slate and read outputs before scheduling anything, never assume it is empty.

Re-uploading fixed it. The gate worked; the upload script's own success output is NOT evidence. ALWAYS confirm with hosting_listWebsiteFilesAndDirectoriesV1 that the staged files exist at the exact local byte sizes BEFORE scheduling stage. The failed attempt coincided with a hosting_createAccountCronJobV1 call returning all-empty fields ({uid:'',username:'',time:'',command:''}) and a cron that was never created (slate empty) — treat an empty-field create response as a FAILURE, verify with listAccountCronJobsV1, and retry.

blocker_found_2026_09_21: While starting the production QA, every request from the QA machine returned HTTP 429 with an empty body and Server: cloudflare. The site's nameservers had been changed to Cloudflare (marek/nataly.ns.cloudflare.com, zone created 2026-09-21T09:26Z, activated 09:37Z) OUTSIDE this session; Phase B (Cloudflare migration) had been left read-only-pending. Cloudflare GraphQL analytics show edgeResponseStatus 429 == originResponseStatus 429 (206 on provatferi.org, 7 on admin in the prior 6h, alongside 489+ successful 200s): the 429s come from the ORIGIN (Hostinger), not from any Cloudflare rule — the zone has no custom WAF/rate-limit rules. Working hypothesis, NOT proven: Hostinger's per-client-IP limiting now sees Cloudflare's shared edge IPs instead of individual visitors, so a burst of QA traffic exhausted a shared allowance. Whether real visitors were also receiving 429 is UNKNOWN. Read-only findings on the Cloudflare zone vs the pre-migration backup: MX/SPF changed to Google Workspace (smtp.google.com / _spf.google.com, plus a Google site-verification TXT and a stricter DMARC) — apparently deliberate — while this app still sends through Hostinger SMTP, so SPF (~all) and strict DMARC alignment (aspf=s) are likely to fail for app mail; DKIM CNAMEs (hostingermail-a/b/c._domainkey), autoconfig, autodiscover and ftp are proxied (orange-cloud) though they must be DNS-only; www still CNAMEs to a *.cdn.hstgr.net Hostinger CDN host (double CDN); http3 is ON although it was to stay OFF for the ISP baseline; ssl mode is 'full' not 'full (strict)'. No Cloudflare or DNS change was made by this session.
